correction_scope: The earlier interpretation used the Kyrgyzstan April 2024 TikTok TLS-timeout finding as mechanism-compatible evidence for the historically known PROTEI_DPI network MegaCom/AS50223. Raw ASN-resolved OONI measurements show this attribution of the TLS-timeout mechanism to AS50223 was incorrect.

AS50223_MegaCom.additional_root_tiktok_measurement: DNS android_dns_cache_no_data for A and AAAA

corrected_claims: April 2024 Kyrgyzstan TikTok blocking was implemented heterogeneously across measured ASNs.
The post-ClientHello/TLS-timeout measurements in the acquired sample belong to AS47237, not MegaCom/AS50223.
AS50223 therefore cannot be used from this event as a PROTEI TLS-timeout reference.
AS50223 DNS blocking must not be labeled a PROTEI fingerprint because the measurement does not identify the enforcement product and the documented PROTEI deployment is historical (2014-2015).
rejected_claims: KNOWN PROTEI DPI network AS50223 -> 2024 measured TLS timeout
The 2024 TikTok TLS timeout provides a MegaCom/PROTEI reference fingerprint
Similarity between Cuba RST and Kyrgyzstan TLS timeout supports Cuba->PROTEI through AS50223
surviving_claims: MegaCom/AS50223 is an independently documented historical PROTEI_DPI deployment.
PROTEI_DPI is technically capable of filtering and policy enforcement.
Cuba/AS27725 has raw OONI evidence of rapid reset-like TLS failures after ClientHello during the July 2021 Signal restriction window.
The Cuba->PROTEI device bridge remains open and requires a genuinely discriminating PROTEI reference or direct device/deployment evidence.
epistemic_lesson: National censorship policy and generic DPI failure type are insufficient for vendor attribution. ASN-resolved raw measurements are mandatory before using a network as a vendor fingerprint reference.
